title: This Bourbon Vanilla Tallow Balm Is Weird. My Skin Loves It.
body:
Okay so I’m sitting here with my face feeling… good. That’s the word. Just good. It’s a Tuesday night, I think, and I just smeared some of that beef tallow balm on my face. The bourbon vanilla one. Sounds insane, right? Putting rendered cow fat on your skin. I thought it was the weirdest thing I’d ever ordered off Etsy. But my knuckles were cracking from the spring wind, like that dry, weird air that’s still cold but the sun’s out, you know? And I was desperate. So I opened the jar. And now it’s just part of the whole… thing. My tallow balm routine. That’s a sentence I never thought I’d type.

It started last month. My elbows were like sandpaper. My face felt tight all the time, no matter how much of that expensive blue lotion I used. The one in the fancy bottle that costs as much as a decent takeout order. Did nothing. Zip. So I was scrolling, half-watching some baking show, and I kept seeing this tallow skincare stuff. Beef tallow. For your face. I was like, okay, the internet has officially lost it. But the reviews were all these normal people saying it fixed their dry skin. And the bourbon vanilla scent sounded… less barnyard than I feared. So I clicked buy. From this little shop in France, I think. Waited like two weeks for it to show up.

## How This Beef Tallow Stuff Ended Up on My Nightstand

The box was small. Unassuming. I opened it and there was this little glass jar. It looked… fine. Normal. I unscrewed the lid and poked it. The texture was weird. Not bad weird. It’s like this whipped beef tallow balm, they take the suet from grass-fed cows and whip it until it’s this fluffy, creamy… stuff. It’s solid but soft, like cold butter but lighter. You scoop a tiny bit with your finger and it just melts. I held it up to my nose. Smelled like vanilla maybe? Or not. Something. Not like cake. Deeper. Like vanilla extract your grandma had in the back of the cupboard forever. Warm. It was actually kind of nice. Cozy. My cat, Mochi, jumped up to sniff it and then gave me this look of utter betrayal before stalking off. Judgmental little fluff.

I was skeptical. Big time. But my hands were a disaster. So I took a pea-sized amount—seriously, you need so little—and rubbed it between my palms. It went from this solid balm to this silky oil almost instantly. No greasy film. I just worked it into the back of my hands and over my knuckles. Cold at first. Then not. I don’t know how to describe it. It just sank in. Like, really sank in. Ten minutes later, I was typing and I looked at my hands and they just looked… normal. Not shiny. Not crackly. Just skin. But better skin. I kept flexing my fingers, waiting for that tight feeling. It never came.

## My Actual Daily Skincare with Tallow (It’s Not Fancy)

So here’s how I use it now. It’s not some 12-step thing. I’m not that person. My routine is basically: try not to fall asleep with my makeup on. But this tallow balm snuck in.

At night, after I wash my face—I use that cheap drugstore cleanser in the green bottle, whatever—I’ll pat my face dry. Not bone dry, just damp. Then I grab the jar. I scoop out maybe half a pea for my whole face. I rub it between my fingertips to warm it up and then just… press it in. On my cheeks, my forehead, around my eyes. I don’t rub hard, just kind of pat and press. It feels like nothing after a minute. Like I didn’t put anything on. But my skin feels… calm. That’s the only word. Not moisturized in a slick way. Just calm. Like it can finally relax. Sometimes I put a tiny bit more on any super dry patches. I had this red, flaky spot near my eyebrow from the wind, and I’d put a dab on it before bed. Gone in like, three days.

In the morning, if my skin feels tight (which it hasn’t lately, weirdly), I’ll use an even tinier amount. Like, a grain-of-rice amount. Just to take the edge off before I put on sunscreen. It plays nice with my sunscreen. Doesn’t pill or anything.

But my favorite use? My elbows and knees. Oh man. Spring is brutal. You start wearing short sleeves again and you realize your elbows look like they belong to a desert lizard. So after my shower, when I’m still in the bathroom with the mirror all fogged up, I’ll scoop a bit more—maybe a whole pea—and really work it into one elbow. Then the other. Then my knees. It absorbs so fast. I can put my pajamas on right after and they don’t stick to me. It’s magic. Or science. They say it mimics human skin sebum, so it absorbs deep. I don’t know about all that. I just know it works.

## What Actually Happened After a Few Weeks

So I’ve been using this bourbon vanilla tallow balm for… a month? Maybe five weeks. I’m bad with time. But here’s the weird part. I stopped thinking about my skin. That’s the biggest change. I used to be constantly aware of that tight feeling on my cheeks, or my hands feeling like paper. Now I just… don’t. I catch my reflection sometimes and my face just looks even. Not oily. Not dry. Just even. My makeup goes on smoother, which is a bonus I didn’t expect.

I was at my mom’s last weekend and she grabbed my hand and was like, “Your hands are so soft, what are you using?” And I had to say, “Uh, cow fat.” She looked at me like I’d grown a second head. But I showed her the jar. She smelled it. She poked it. She was skeptical, just like I was. But I left it with her. Told her to try it on her knuckles. Got a text two days later: “Okay fine. Where do I get one?” So I sent her the Etsy link. The shop is called Pure Sway or something like that. They just make this stuff. Simple.

It’s not a miracle cure. I still get a pimple if I eat too much pizza. But that dry, itchy, uncomfortable feeling that used to follow me around all spring? Gone. Completely. My skin just feels… fortified. Like it can handle the weird spring weather now. I’m probably gonna order another jar soon. I’m only halfway through this one because you need so little, but I don’t want to run out.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly, it is. From what I read, it’s really similar to the oils our own skin makes. So it doesn’t just sit on top—it actually gets absorbed and helps your skin barrier. My face definitely thinks it’s good.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was terrified of this. I have combo skin that can get clogged easy. But this stuff? It just disappears. It’s not pore-clogging at all. It’s the opposite—it seems to calm everything down. My skin feels clearer, if that makes sense.

**What does the bourbon vanilla tallow balm smell like?**
It’s not food vanilla. It’s not sweet. It’s like… a warm, deep vanilla. Like the scent of a vanilla bean pod, not ice cream. It’s subtle. Fades pretty quick after you put it on. Just leaves a faint, cozy smell that’s really comforting, especially at night.

Anyway. If your skin is feeling angry with the season change, or just perpetually dry and nothing helps, this might be worth a shot. It’s a weird little jar of magic from France. I’m a convert. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. That’s the whole review, I guess.
random_tangent: I should probably order another jar soon
